subject: computer-science
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Structured query language (SQL): inserting and pattern matching

questions.q: Which statement best describes a primary key in a relational database?
options: A field that uniquely identifies each record in a table
A field that links to a separate database file
A field that is allowed to contain duplicate values
The first field entered into any table
questions.explain: A primary key is a unique identifier that distinguishes every record in a table.

questions.q: What is a foreign key?
options: A field in one table that refers to the primary key of another table
A primary key that has been duplicated within the same table
A field that must always store numeric data
A key that encrypts the contents of a field
questions.explain: A foreign key stores a primary key value from another table to create a link between the two tables.

questions.q: In a relational database table, a single row is known as a...
questions.explain: Each row in a table represents one record (an entity such as one pupil or one product).

questions.q: In a database table, a column that stores one item of data about each record is called a...
questions.explain: A field (attribute) is a single column holding one type of data for every record.

questions.q: What is a key advantage of a relational database over a single flat file?
options: It reduces data redundancy by storing data in separate linked tables
It always runs faster on any hardware
It removes the need for keys entirely
It can only store text data
questions.explain: Splitting data into linked tables avoids storing the same information repeatedly, reducing redundancy.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a foreign key?
options: To create a relationship (link) between two tables
To sort records into alphabetical order
questions.explain: A foreign key links a record in one table to a related record in another, forming a relationship.

questions.q: Which SQL keyword specifies the table that data is retrieved from?
questions.explain: FROM names the table(s) that the query draws its data from.

questions.q: Which SQL keyword is used to specify a condition that records must meet?
questions.explain: WHERE filters records so only those meeting the stated condition are returned.

questions.q: Which SQL clause is used to sort the results of a query?
questions.explain: ORDER BY sorts the returned records, ascending (ASC) by default or descending (DESC).

questions.q: Which SQL keyword is used with a wildcard to search for a pattern within text?
questions.explain: LIKE combined with a wildcard such as % matches text against a pattern.

questions.q: What does adding DESC to an ORDER BY clause do?
options: Sorts the results into descending order
questions.explain: DESC sorts results from highest to lowest (e.g. Z to A or largest number first).

questions.q: What does SELECT * mean in an SQL query?
options: Select all fields (columns) from the table
Multiply the values in the fields
questions.explain: The asterisk is a wildcard meaning every field in the specified table.

questions.q: Given a table Students(Name, Age), which query returns the names of students older than 16?
options: SELECT Name FROM Students WHERE Age > 16
SELECT Age FROM Students WHERE Name > 16
SELECT Name WHERE Age > 16 FROM Students
FIND Name IN Students WHERE Age > 16
questions.explain: The correct order is SELECT field FROM table WHERE condition, filtering on Age greater than 16.

questions.q: What does the query SELECT Surname FROM Pupils ORDER BY Surname ASC return?
options: All pupils' surnames sorted A to Z
All pupils' surnames sorted Z to A
Only one surname from the table
questions.explain: ASC sorts the returned surnames in ascending (A to Z) order.

questions.q: Which SQL statement is used to add a new record to a table?
questions.explain: INSERT INTO adds a new row of data to a table.

questions.q: Which is the correct general form of an SQL statement to add a record?
options: INSERT INTO table (field1, field2) VALUES (value1, value2)
questions.explain: INSERT INTO lists the fields, then VALUES lists the matching data to store.

questions.q: For a table Members(ID, Name), which statement correctly adds a new record?
questions.explain: Fields are listed after the table name and their values after VALUES, with text in quotes.

questions.q: In a WHERE clause, when are records returned if two conditions are joined by AND?
options: Only when both conditions are true
When at least one condition is true
When the two conditions are identical
questions.explain: AND requires every joined condition to be true for a record to be returned.

questions.q: Which surnames match the condition WHERE Surname LIKE 'S%'?
options: Surnames that start with the letter S
Surnames that end with the letter S
questions.explain: The % wildcard represents any characters, so 'S%' matches any surname beginning with S.

questions.q: In the notation Student(StudentID, Name, Form), where StudentID is underlined, what does the underline indicate?
questions.explain: In this standard notation an underlined field is the table's primary key.
